2026-10-31 Italy

Florence

An early train

We got up bright and early to take the train to Florence.

Rachel half asleep with breakfast

Galleria dell’Accademia

Our first stop in Florence was the Galleria dell’Accademia where we got to see Michelangelo's David and lots of cool paintings. For many paintings, seeing them in person (for non-artsy people like us) is not too different from seeing a photo online. However, for a sculpture like the David, it was really cool to see it in person. It is 5+ meters tall and the details were exquisite.

Stradivari violin!
God is often depicted with the Alpha and Omega
An unfinished sculpture of Matthew by Michelangelo
Close up of David's face. The pupils are heart-shaped.
Kid with dog
Commissioned by a man to depict his wife’s last moments with his son.
This painting from the 1300s shows many different stories from the Gospels.

Gelato

We got gelato. It was sooo delicious.

Santa Maria del Fiore

After the museum we went to the Basilica de Santa Maria del Fiore which hosts Florence’s iconic dome. They began building the church in the late 1200s and knew that they wanted to build a gigantic dome. However, at the time they didn't have the technology to do so. Regardless, they began building the rest of the church, confident that eventually they would figure it out. About 200 years later, they finally found someone who could build the dome and successfully finished the church.

the dome from inside

Basilica di Santa Croce

Our next stop was the Basilica di Santa Croce. Built by Franciscan monks in the 1200s, this church is the burial place of many of Italy's greats. The floor was covered with tombs. Along the sides of the room were the tombs and monuments of people like Machiavelli, Galileo Galilei, Michelangelo, Leonardo Da Vinci, Dante.

An original coat of St Francis of Assisi.
Donatello painting.
Tomb of Machiavelli
Monument to Dante (he is buried in a different city since he was exiled...)
Tomb of Michelangelo
Tomb of Galileo Galilei
Monument to Leonardo Da Vinci

Lunch

Lunch was delicious! Sebastian got a seafood risotto and Rachel got traditional Florence Pappa al Pomodoro. We got panna cotta for dessert.

Palazzo Vecchio and Porcellino

We then walked through Palazzo Vecchio. It has replicas of important statues.

Hercules killing a giant (not sure why he is bigger than the giant)
Samson killing a philistine with a donkey's jawbone.
Perseus killing Medusa
Rachel with real Porcellino

Across the river and up the hill

From there we crossed the river on a beautiful bridge lined with jewelry shops. This part of town was gorgeous. We headed to the top of a hill for photos during the sunset.

Don't know how those are holding there...
The Cupola is huge!

Dessert and dinner

For dinner we had Florence's Bistecca alla Fiorentina!

Tiramisu
